fullText:
Agent 说“验证完了”，怎么才能真的信它？

很多朋友都被 Agent 坑过：它信誓旦旦说做好了、验证完了，你信以为真，上线后发现压根没做好。被老板骂完回头找它，它认错态度很好，下次还是一样。

问题出在我们让它验证的方式上：Agent 不知道什么叫“做好了”，你也没有低成本的办法确认它真的做好了。分享五条我在用 Agent 做验证时的经验。

一、不要依赖对抗式验证

对抗式验证就是让另一个甚至多个 Agent 来检查结果，执行的 Agent 根据反馈改进，再检查、再改进，直到完成为止。

听起来很好，实际上经常无法收敛。尤其是不太聪明的模型，大部分时候是越改越糟，还浪费了很多 Token。

原因是缺少统一的验收标准。负责检查的 Agent 并不一定知道完整的上下文，也不知道准确的验收标准，于是自作主张提一堆意见，执行的 Agent 再照单全收，结果就越改越偏。

二、给出清晰的验收标准，再给一个能验收的环境

举个例子，你把设计稿交给 Agent，说：“帮我把这几个设计稿做成页面”，通常它会给你一个差不多的结果，有时候出入还很大。

换一个说法：“帮我把这几个设计稿做成页面，完成后请对网页截图，对比设计稿，要求像素一个都不要差”。这时候 Agent 做完不会轻易交差，它会截图，写工具对比截图和设计稿的像素差异，返工重做，直到像素真的一个都不差。

大部分时候我们并不需要一个像素都不差，有些偏差可以接受。重点是让它知道验收标准是什么，并且手里有办法自己去验。

三、越早验证，返工成本越低

尽早验证在传统软件工程里是常识，是大量血泪教训换来的。只是现在 Vibe Coding 让生成代码的成本大幅降低，非专业人士越来越多，大家渐渐忘了写代码之前还有三道关：

可行性分析：这个项目真的值得做吗？做出来会有人用吗？投入产出比合算吗？

原型开发：先做基本的交互，用模拟数据低成本做出一个可运行的原型，快速验证方向对不对，不对马上调整。现在 Agent 做原型已经很强了，比如 Claude Design（或者本地版的 https://t.co/QVpnqsxzMD），做出来的东西和最终结果看起来没什么差别，成本低得多，速度也快。

系统设计：技术选型、模块划分、数据结构、数据库设计、API Schema 这些。设计没做好，系统也能跑，但将来维护成本要高不少。Agent 能力虽然强，选的技术方案并不总是最好的。动手实现之前，先让它写一份技术方案文档，你大概看看：一方面帮你理解项目是怎么实现的，另一方面能及时纠正潜在问题，避免做完再返工。

四、让 Agent 提供证据，降低你的验收成本

人在 Loop 里是必不可少的，完全交给 AI，大概率只能收获 AI Slop。但人的验收能力是瓶颈，要确认的东西太多会很累。我最近用 Antigravity，跨 Workspace 每读一个文件都要我手工确认一遍，简直快崩溃了。

所以要把人确认的成本降到最低：能快速判断结果对不对，快速指出哪里有问题。

最简单的方式，是让 Agent 提供截图、录屏、可视化的 HTML 报告。Agent 在截图过程中自己也能发现一些问题，但截图最大的价值，是让人一眼就能看出问题。

想象一下，你是老板，员工来汇报工作，一页密密麻麻的 Word 文档和三页漂亮的 PPT，哪个更容易看？

我现在最常用的几个做法：

- 开发新功能，让它提供新功能的截图
- 修 bug，让它提供修改前和修改后的截图对比
- 让它自己模拟 API 响应数据，动态生成各种不同场景的截图，完全不需要服务端配合（虽然我还没搞明白它是怎么模拟的）

五、代码审查聚焦于真正的问题

Agent 生成代码的速度太快，瓶颈已经转移到了代码审查和验证上。代码审查不太可能完全靠人来做了，但人参与仍然有意义，只是方式要调整：

- PR 尽可能小。这样 Agent 审起来准确率更高，人也看得过来。
- 让 Agent 审，但不全信它的结论。审查结果要分级，人只盯 P0、P1 级别的问题，尤其是安全和性能问题，人工甄别一下，必要时让 Agent 解读、在本地验证。
- 细枝末节放过去。代码规范、最佳实践这类问题，不用太在意。

最后

这五条说的是同一件事：Agent 说的“做好了”不能直接当结论用，得让它变成你能检查的东西。

- 动手之前，告诉它什么叫做好了
- 动手之前，先用原型和方案文档把方向验一遍
- 做完之后，让它拿截图和对比来证明
- 你自己的精力，只花在最要紧的问题上

fullText:
Interesting to hear top mathematicians describe these incredible AI achievements in math as "just evals for AI researchers". 

There are many takeaways, but the one I stick with is the importance of ambitious evals in pushing what's possible in verifiable domains (to advance understanding) and, more importantly, in open-ended domains (to advance real-world applicability). 

I also hear their concern that AI-driven solutions to these math problems aren't leading to much new human understanding of the field. That's an important discussion to have as we figure out how to move forward in the new era of accelerated discoveries. 

The evolved role of the practitioner or scientist is something we are all trying to figure out. As a professional in both, I constantly build for and with AI agents. I spend a lot of time augmenting my knowledge and toolbox with AI and developing a ton of evals to improve AI-powered systems for all kinds of work. This is helping me understand the world around me (economy, physics, health, people, networks, etc.) and prepare better for this new era of intelligent computer systems. 

Like Terence Tao, I believe in the Copernican view of intelligence: a richer, broader view that advocates for different forms of intelligence to coexist. Although not positioned this way (unfortunately), I believe the researchers making these breakthroughs in math with AI are the first signs of that. The quicker we can adapt, the more problems we can attempt to solve—hopefully with a sharper focus on real-world problems affecting the world today.

Just thinking out loud about the current state of things, and hopefully offering words of encouragement to the younger practitioners and scientists who may feel lost about all that's happening today.

fullText: My personal design esthetic is homeless Batman

Here is my initial FSD v15 review after driving with it all afternoon and evening:

First off, Elon was right. This update is a BANGER! Tesla Reality View is out of this world and so insanely cool I’m still trying to process it all. 

FSD V15.0.1 brings so many improvements behind the scenes, in addition to the wildly cool UI. 

Tesla Reality View IS AMAZING! Pictures and video don’t do it any justice, this is something that has to be experienced to truly understand. Got to take a few friends tonight on drives to show them and every single person was blown away by it. The amount of detail it shows and generates is wild and so impressive. It shows reflection in the car, buildings, trees, turn arrows on the display and more. 

FSD v15 now has pothole avoidance! I had it swerve and avoid/straddle a few potholes tonight that were difficult for me to see in the dark.

Another great new feature in FSD v15 is speed camera slowdown. As you approach a speed camera, it automatically slows smoothly to the speed limit if you are in a quicker profile. This is a huge quality of life improvement especially as more cities get speed cameras. 

Parking seems near unchanged from the last build, I feel it picking spots quicker especially at the supercharger I went to tonight. Seems to be preferring to park in the first or second open spot it sees which is great, but it tried to park in one handicap spot- otherwise good. By far, the coolest part is Tesla Reality View. Holy crap is it insane to watch while parking. It’s the best backup/360 camera money can buy and such a detailed and clear view. 

Another new change I haven’t seen many people talk about is the turn signal fade. On FSD, the turn signal sound gets quieter after a few clicks. This is so nice if you’re sitting at a red light and makes drives more peaceful. 

Quiet Mode is also so nice at night. It darkens the display and just shows arrival time; music, climate on the bottom and a quick grok button on the top. Another feature that makes it feel like a Robotaxi UI and a peaceful supervising experience.

Another improvement is much better handling of dips and speed bumps. The past couple updates it’s been a bit too fast in my Model Y, and it’s now so smooth.

The nag is definitely reduced. The last couple versions of v14.3 had been sometimes a bit strict, but definitely more relaxed in v15.0.1. Another thing I noticed is way less wiper washing, a very welcome change. 

Personalized parking preferences are SO cool. At home, I can click on a person icon on the map and choose street parking or driveway, and it backs into the driveway EXACTLY in the spot I park my Model Y. It leared where I park and knows it. 

It also now lets you choose which lot you want to park in if the mall or store has multiple lots, you can select it on the map, worked at the mall, Costco, and Home Depot tonight. 

I need to touch on Tesla Reality View again because it’s just that cool. It really feels like you’re in a video game like NFS or GTA. I’m blown away by this and didn’t expect it at all. Tesla teams COOKED with it, I’ve seen so many on X now wanting Teslas because of it. I drove down Rodeo Drive tonight as well as by the SpaceX Falcon 9 and the views were so cool. Another place it’s cool is in wooded areas or tree filled streets, the way it shows everything is spectacular. Parking garages also give a cool look to them with the roof incorporated into the top of the UI. I didn’t think FSD could get this much better, as it was already so good and it did. 

I absolutely can’t wait to see what else is coming in the future and driving this more on road trips.

@elonmusk, you were right- V15 is incredible and super human! Huge congrats to the Tesla team on this, what a sick update. @TeslaSI and UI teams did a fantastic job, thank you all.

fullText:
About the apparent Riemann Hypothesis proof...

1) Wow!  Congratulations!  Amazing!  I've been waiting for this for literally half a century... it was always clear this would be possible and now , finally, it is...

2) A new era of math is upon us, but in the end just a special case of a new era of almost everything -- aka yes indeed ladies and jellyspoons the Singularity really is near...

3) Of course proving RH with human assistance (or without for that matter) does not mean you have human-level AGI, which involves qualitatively different capabilities than amazing expert performance in any collection of pretrained domains...

4) On a personal level yes it's also slightly annoying.  Not because as a mathematician I am jealous of AIs for being in some ways better at math than me.   More-so because I'm jealous of the folks at Big Tech labs for having the resource to spend huge amounts of $$ on tokens for pursuing speculative math proofs !!!

I had my own half-baked interesting direction for proving RH, along with other epic proofs like P \neq NP, the remaining bit of Navier-Stokes existence/uniqueness. YM mass gap, and more.  Whether my ideas on these were right I don't know -- I played around with current LLMs + Lean to help me flesh out my ideas and they are awesome and seemed to be making progress, but I just don't have enough budget to put in a huge amount of tokens to run huge proof search trees on these things..

So now we are in a brief math era where the glory does to those with a mix of creative insights and a fuckload of tokens and compute to spare...

"Brief" because the capabilities will go up and the price will come down and pretty soon proving historically epic math theorems will be a commodity like making web apps or writing articles or "composing songs in a genre" are now... and then there will be not so much glory left in finishing off human math ... 

... but there will be a question of who develops the next phase of posthuman math -- A) AI agents owned by a few big companies working closely w/ gov't agencies, and/or, B) AI agents owned and coordinated by a decentralized and diverse network of human (and then AI) parties...

And yeah, I'm working hard on securing a lot more compute for my AGI R&D team ... but when I get it, I will spend it on rapidly building toward beneficial AGI not on proving famous math theorems... it's all fun and important but getting AGI/ASI/RSI right is more important than any other technological feat on the planet right now...   (though yeah if I were as rich as Anthropic I would probably do both.. 8-D ... I get it...)

fullText:
listening to men like elon, ilya, or sam, you can sense a twinge of relief, that the utter absurdity and terrible magnificence that have been driving them near crazy their entire lives is slowly becoming universal, that the sheer derealization (which drives one to believe their life is too odd to not be some strange prank or simulation) that comes naturally with being the one monkey in eight billion, no, a hundred and seventeen billion (to ever live), strapped to the launch chair at the end of the world, is infecting the rest of us: a strangeness that has been building since maybe the dawn of agriculture, or fire, and finally coming to an unignorable global front. welcome to the technological singularity.

Terrence McKenna: “It’s only going to get weirder. The level of contradiction is going to rise excruciatingly, even beyond the excruciating present levels of contradiction. So I think it’s just going to get weirder and weirder and weirder. And finally, it’s going to be so weird that people are going to have to talk about how weird it is. And at that point, novelty theory can come out of the woods. Because eventually people are going to say, “What the hell is going on?” It’s just too nuts! It’s not enough to say it’s nuts, you have to explain why it’s so nuts.

So between now and 2012, the next fourteen years, I look for the invention of artificial life, the cloning of human beings, possible contact with extraterrestrials, possible human immortality, and at the same time, appalling acts of brutality, genocide, race-baiting, homophobia, famine, starvation—because the systems which are in place to keep the world sane are utterly inadequate to the forces that have been unleashed. The collapse of the socialist world, the rise of the Internet—these are changes so immense, nobody could imagine them ever happening. And now that they have happened, nobody even bothers to mention what a big deal it is. The fact that there is no such thing as the Soviet Union—people never talk about it anymore. But when I was a kid, the notion that that would ever change was beyond conceiving….

The mushroom said to me once, it said, “This is what it’s like when a species prepares to depart for the stars.” You don’t depart for the stars under calm and orderly conditions. It’s a fire in a madhouse. And that’s what we have: the fire in the madhouse at the end of time. This is what it’s like when a species prepares to move on to the next dimension. The entire destiny of all life on the planet is tied up in this. We are not acting for ourselves or from ourselves. We happen to be the point species on a transformation that will affect every living organism on this planet at its conclusion.”
